title: Usage-limit reset reported after an apparent outage-compensation action
summary: A public Codex issue reported weekly usage returning to 100% and the renewal date moving without intervening use. An OpenAI repository contributor explained that this behavior occurs when usage limits are reset and that resets are sometimes used to compensate users after outages. This supports an inferred reset, not a confirmed personal observation in this project.

cause.rationale: An OpenAI repository contributor described outage compensation as a reason these resets are occasionally performed, but did not identify a specific incident for this event.

detectionSignals: Weekly usage remaining rises to 100% without corresponding inactivity-window expiry.
The displayed renewal or reset date moves forward at the same time.
Several independent public reports cluster in a short period.
An OpenAI staff or official status source attributes the change to a reset.
contradictions: The public report did not provide a machine-verifiable exact reset timestamp.
No specific OpenAI Status incident was linked to the reset.

title: Early weekly-limit reset corroborated by an OpenAI repository contributor
summary: A public Codex issue reported that a weekly limit reset many hours before the displayed reset time. An OpenAI repository contributor stated that this was the intended result of a limit reset: usage returns to 100% remaining and the time window restarts. The event is retained as inferred history because it was not submitted and verified as a personal observation through this project.

cause.rationale: An OpenAI repository contributor confirmed the mechanism and intended behavior, but the public record did not state why this particular reset was initiated.

detectionSignals: Usage remaining returns to 100% before the previously displayed reset time.
The usage window restarts and a new future reset timestamp appears.
Contemporaneous reports from multiple surfaces can distinguish a broad reset from an account-specific display issue.
contradictions: The report supplied only an approximate local event time and did not state its time zone.
The public record did not establish affected-plan scope or the reason for the reset.

title: Plus and Pro limits reset after a promotional-limit application bug
summary: An OpenAI repository contributor reported that a defect had prevented a two-times promotional limit increase from applying for an estimated subset of Plus and Pro users. After public reports and attempted mitigations, the contributor stated that the issue was fixed and that rate limits were being reset for all Plus and Pro users as compensation. This remains inferred history because it was not submitted and verified through this project's observation process.

cause.assessment: Compensation after a promotional-limit application bug
cause.rationale: An OpenAI repository contributor explicitly identified the defect, affected plan tiers, estimated affected share, fix, and compensating reset.

detectionSignals: A staff statement identifies a usage-entitlement defect and announces a compensating reset.
Plus and Pro users see remaining rate limits restored after the fix.
The reset timestamp or usage window restarts near the staff announcement.
Reports of unexpectedly rapid limit consumption decline after the fix.
contradictions: The staff statement estimated that the underlying defect affected 9% of Plus and Pro users, while the compensating reset was described as applying to all users on those two plans.
The public record does not provide a machine-verifiable completion timestamp for every affected account.

title: Weekly usage reset to compensate for a user-impacting incident
summary: A public Codex issue reported a weekly reset occurring earlier than the displayed time. An OpenAI repository contributor explained that an incident had affected some users earlier that day and that weekly usage was reset for all users as compensation, restoring remaining usage and restarting the weekly window on next use. The event is retained as inferred history rather than a confirmed model label.

cause.rationale: An OpenAI repository contributor explicitly attributed the reset to compensation for an incident, but the public comment did not identify a corresponding permanent OpenAI Status incident URL.

detectionSignals: Weekly usage remaining returns to 100% before the displayed reset time.
The weekly usage window restarts on the next Codex use.
A staff statement links the reset to incident compensation.
A matching official incident transition would strengthen future attribution.
contradictions: The public report supplied approximate local times without a stated time zone.
No permanent OpenAI Status incident record was located for the incident referenced by the contributor.
The contributor described the incident as affecting some users but the compensating reset as applying to all users; affected-plan scope was not stated.
